breakdown.description: The prompt uses the polar moment J in the Euler buckling check, even though Euler buckling is governed by the flexural second moment I, not torsional rigidity.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses I = (π d^4)/64 for the Euler buckling calculation, not the polar moment J = (π d^4)/32. It explicitly notes that J is not used in the Euler buckling calculation, directly correcting the original error of using the polar moment instead of the second moment of area.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats a satisfactory average-stress yield check as if it ruled out buckling, even though a column may buckle before reaching the material yield stress.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification treats yielding and Euler buckling as two independent checks, comparing both σ_avg/Sy and P/P_cr as separate utilization ratios to determine which is more critical. It does not treat a satisfactory yield check as sufficient to rule out buckling, correctly aligning with the ground truth approach where both checks must be evaluated independently.
